sections_target.text: This document describes the steps of the annual maintenance of liquid batteries, which is considered one of the most important maintenance activities required for batteries of all types. All operations are carried out on them to return the batteries to the optimum operating condition and the required efficiency and to continuously verify their fitness for service as required at the time of their initial installation. The attached forms show how to carry out the major overhaul and measure the efficiency.

The first draft was prepared by Eng. Saad Mahmoud Mohamed Bassiouny, reviewed by Eng. Adel Abdel Qader El-Nagar of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, Accountant, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.

According to the type of batteries, certain conditions must be observed for the batteries to work with high efficiency: charging must be continuous to compensate for losses, and this charger must be suitable for the voltage and current of the batteries. It is also important that the loads suit the design of the batteries, together with the number of operating hours the batteries are required to work for.

Batteries are an independent voltage source. The idea of using liquid acid batteries in power stations arose because of the great danger when power is interrupted or problems occur in the electrical networks, and the need of some auxiliaries to continue operating, such as the standby oil pumps for turbines or the various cooling equipment, as well as emergency lighting.

These batteries were therefore manufactured in different types, including dry, acid and alkaline batteries, all of which depend on chemical reactions which ultimately produce the negative and positive electrodes that cause a current to flow between the electrodes and a voltage difference.

From this we see that the formation of the electrodes and the discharge of the charges generated by the chemical reactions require that these batteries be provided with what restores their charge and allows them to be reused — what we call chargers. Thus we use the batteries many times while maintaining their safety and always verifying their fitness for service and carrying out the maintenance needed for them to remain fit for service.

In preparation for measuring the efficiency of the batteries, the batteries have been calibrated in terms of concentration and tested as previously described in the first item, and the internal resistance has also been determined and verified as suitable. Returning again to the original condition the battery was designed for, according to the manufacturer's standard specifications, we have the following information: battery voltage, battery current, number of operating hours, and the loads for which the batteries are used.
Therefore, after verifying the battery voltage and current, the battery is loaded with the required loads and the voltage and current readings are taken according to the following table:
By recording the data in the table, any changes that occur can be written in the remarks column.

From the observations we find the start of the voltage drop down to 85% of the rated voltage; we then have the number of operating hours, and thus we find that the number of operating hours is in good condition. By comparing it with the number of hours the battery was designed for, the efficiency can thus be measured.
In this case, the efficiency is compared as the number of operating hours in good condition divided by the number of operating hours the batteries were designed for, to give the required efficiency.

Introduction
This document describes the steps of the annual maintenance of liquid batteries, which is considered one of the most important maintenance activities required for batteries of all types. All operations are carried out on them to return the batteries to the optimum operating condition and the required efficiency and to continuously verify their fitness for service as required at the time of their initial installation. The attached forms show how to carry out the major overhaul and measure the efficiency.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Saad Mahmoud Mohamed Bassiouny, reviewed by Eng. Adel Abdel Qader El-Nagar of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company, endorsed by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Director of Inspection and Quality Control, and approved by Mr. Mahmoud Mohamed Soliman, Accountant, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and Supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
How batteries work:
According to the type of batteries, certain conditions must be observed for the batteries to work with high efficiency: charging must be continuous to compensate for losses, and this charger must be suitable for the voltage and current of the batteries. It is also important that the loads suit the design of the batteries, together with the number of operating hours the batteries are required to work for.
Batteries are an independent voltage source. The idea of using liquid acid batteries in power stations arose because of the great danger when power is interrupted or problems occur in the electrical networks, and the need of some auxiliaries to continue operating, such as the standby oil pumps for turbines or the various cooling equipment, as well as emergency lighting.

Thus we use the batteries many times while maintaining their safety and always verifying their fitness for service and carrying out the maintenance needed for them to remain fit for service.
